tasks.task: Turn a rough request into a role brief and search plan

items.when: When the client decides to fill a role and you need every step to an accepted offer
When a manager's rough ask must become a one-page brief and a dated search plan
Before agreeing pay and timing, to see pay ranges, talent supply and how hard the hire is
When the search needs its channels, timeline and risks written for the hiring manager
When this client has hired badly before, to build the mistakes to rule out this time

tasks.task: Write a role scorecard with mission and outcomes

items.when: When the role needs a mission, six-month outcomes, must-haves and learnables on one page
When the scorecard is a list of duties, to try one built on the problem the hire must solve
When the hire is a salesperson and traits must fit how this firm sells
When the scorecard describes the last person in the job, not the work now needed

tasks.task: Write an honest job post in short and long versions

items.when: When the brief is agreed and you need the post in two lengths with the same facts
When you need a quick clear post with only the real requirements
Before settling the post, to try a version that opens with the problem to solve
When an existing post needs biased or bloated wording found and fixed
Before publishing, to read the post as a good candidate and list what would stop them applying
When the post oversells and an honest admission about the job would build more trust

tasks.task: Plan where the job ad runs and test versions

items.when: When the role needs ad copy, a posting calendar and a test plan across channels
When the role is hard to fill and you want many ad ideas made, with one lead ad chosen
When the ad title is just the job title and you want several angles
Before spending on ads, to test that a candidate can really apply from the link today

tasks.task: Source candidates and build a long list

items.when: Before searching, to picture who fits, where they spend time and what would move them
When you need the best places to look, target companies and a week-by-week plan
When you want profile, search plan and first messages in one guided run
When you need work contacts by role and company to build the long list

tasks.task: Write first messages to people who have not applied

items.when: When you have a short list of people whose public work fits the role
When messages, two follow-ups and answers to common questions must match the post
Before writing, to compare three shapes for the first message and its follow-ups
When one named person needs a personal first message and reply templates
When the approach is on LinkedIn and needs connection notes you send yourself
Before sending, to test each claim in the message against what is really true of the job
When messages sound like spam and need real proof and an easy, honest ask

tasks.task: Set screening criteria and sort applications on evidence

items.when: When criteria and what counts as evidence must be fixed before anyone reads a CV
When you have the job and a pile of resumes and need a shortlist scored only on job needs
When applications come in batches and each batch must be scored the same way
When a strong first impression is deciding the sort before the evidence does

tasks.task: Build a structured interview kit with a scorecard

items.when: When questions and a 1 to 4 scale must follow from the screening criteria
When the stages, who runs each and what each one checks are not yet set
When you need set questions with answer signs for one role quickly
When interviewers need signs of a strong and a weak answer for each question
When each stage needs its own scorecard, a phone screen script and a rating guide
When candidates should show the work, with a scoring guide and fairness checks

tasks.task: Compare finalists and record the hiring decision

items.when: When you want the interviews, work test, comparison and replies in one guided run
When interview notes on several people need a side-by-side on the agreed criteria
When you have notes or transcripts and want the comparison tested for bias
When the panel is rushing to close, to see the pressures bending the choice
When the debrief turns into stories, to score each criterion apart before any overall view

tasks.task: Write reference questions and a call script

items.when: When you need job-related questions with what to listen for in each answer
When you also need a call script and a sheet to record the answers

tasks.task: Draft the offer, check it and plan the offer call

items.when: When terms are agreed and the letter must say exactly what was meant
When you need a letter, pay package and talking points from a role and level
When the candidate may ask for more and you need a package, a plan and call scripts
Before sending, to flag risky terms and non-compete limits for the place of work
When the offer call may stall, to sum up their side and ask calm questions first

tasks.task: Write candidate updates and kind declines for each stage

items.when: When candidates are waiting to hear, or each stage needs a quick, kind and final decline
When one candidate needs a reply that fits exactly where they are in the process
Before sending, to read the decline as the candidate who just spent four hours on a task

tasks.task: Review the candidate experience from apply to offer

items.when: When you need the candidate path mapped, with friction points and a message per stage
After a hire, to survey the manager and candidates and look back at what worked
When applications are low, to test whether the apply link and form work today

tasks.task: Write the weekly hiring progress report

items.when: Every week a role is open, to run the 30-minute review in the same order
When the manager needs where candidates are, where they drop out and what to change
When you have pipeline numbers and want a clear update or chart page for leaders
When time to hire and source measures need defining before anyone reports them

tasks.task: Write a careers page that tells the truth

items.when: When the page must be built from what staff say and what the policies really give
When you have staff interviews or survey comments and need the themes with quotes
Before writing the full page, to see three different first screens as real pages
When the page needs a clear top, proof, answers to doubts and one apply button
When the page is drafted, to see which claims are true and which are dressing
Before it goes live, to tie each perk and promise to a policy or a named staff quote

tasks.task: Write staff stories and posts that show the team at work

items.when: When a staff story or a day at work should become a post or a carousel script
When each story needs an opening line and the first try is a job title
When what you tell candidates and what staff hear may not match
When a story is praise with no moment in it that a reader could picture

tasks.task: Set up a repeatable hiring process and choose an ATS

items.when: When stages and owners from post to offer need fixing for the firm's common roles
When the process must be written down with who does what and the edge cases
When the firm is moving off spreadsheets and must compare tracking systems on the same tasks
When the new process is drafted, to walk one real role through it end to end

tasks.task: Write a hiring manager guide and train interviewers

items.when: When managers need the questions and answer signs in one guide they can hold
When the guide needs a rating scale with an example for each score
When interviewers need a short session with practice, not a document to read

tasks.task: Write a one-page candidate summary for a client

items.when: When an agency sends a shortlist and each summary must be built only from CV and notes
When several summaries go together, to check each person is judged on the same evidence
Before sending, to tie every line about the candidate to the CV or interview notes

tasks.task: Write the weekly hiring update for a client

items.when: When the client needs the week's numbers and what you will change next
When the update should include a clear chart of the pipeline
When the news is bad, to try a version pitched for the person who must hear it
Before sending, to cut recruiter terms the client would not use

tasks.task: Check an AI tool before it screens or ranks candidates

items.when: When an ATS or vendor offers AI screening and you need the questions before switching it on
When the tool needs a test for accuracy and bias and a small pilot with pass rules
When the firm will use AI in hiring and needs a use policy and a notice to candidates

tasks.task: Plan the year's hiring and what it will cost

items.when: When growth goals and a budget must become a role-by-role plan in priority order
When you have headcount history and need a forecast and a monthly cost budget
When finance wants the full yearly cost of one role and hire versus contractor

tasks.task: Hand an accepted hire over to onboarding

items.when: When the offer is accepted and the manager needs a first week planned by half day
When the client wants 90-day goals and one-on-ones set before day one

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real firm, the real role and what was agreed
Before anything reaches a candidate, to cut jargon and inflated wording
Whenever the work states pay, benefits, market figures or legal steps, to give each a source

helpers.when: When the hire needs a contract, a policy answer or a full onboarding plan
When the pay range or offer package needs market data and a band check
When the question is how many people to hire and when, not how to fill one role
When the careers page needs full page copy tested against the apply rate
When job ads need paid reach and targeting on LinkedIn
When employer brand posts need a calendar and a steady run

gaps: No library item writes search strings for job boards, LinkedIn or the open web
No library item builds a career-history interview guide that walks through each past job
No library item sets up an applicant tracking system: stages, email templates and scorecards
No library item writes an employee value promise or a careers page from staff interviews
No library item plans staff story interviews with consent for employer brand use
No library item writes an agency's candidate summary or client update beyond the kit prompts
No library item designs an employee referral scheme; the referral item is for customers
No library item writes a hiring manager guide or trains interviewers in scoring
No library item builds a time-to-hire and source-of-hire report template
No library item makes clearly different versions of a decline note or candidate summary to choose between
No library item writes a warning notice about job scams that use the firm's name
The library has no tool guide for LinkedIn Recruiter, a job board or an applicant tracking system
